title: Product overview — exploration B
summary: Status board: a hero band (DJDL, the one next step as a large button, Verified per platform) over six feature cards, each with its key number and, until Integration is hidden, a sunken integration well that asks the same three questions in every card.
compare: Two blocks and an aside, no table: the hero band, then Features (a 3 × 2 board at desktop and wide, 2 × 3 at tablet, one column on phone), then Recent activity (the 400px aside at wide, spanning both blocks; below the board under 1600px).

Hero, left pane: DJDL's logo, name, slug and identity line ('A DJ app for macOS and Windows') with ⋯ More at the end of the row; 32px under it the next step: the Warning pill and 'Managed config' subject, the statement 'Required secret identity.acoustidKey has no value in the Default profile.' at 18/24, and 'Set secret' as the page's one primary (40px, full width on phone). A faint warning wash rises from the pane's lower left while the next step is an issue.

The next step is computed: the first Needs-attention item, else the first open console step in canonical order (today, after the secret: Ship builds › Add Sparkle signing key), else the first enabled feature's main action. There is no separate Needs attention card and no 'Continue integration' button; with two or more attention items the pill counts them and the statement shows the first.

Hero, right pane: Integration (16/24) with a ghost 'Hide' (eye-off, aria-label 'Hide Integration'), offered because macOS has a Verified feature and never automatic. macOS: name, '2 of 5 verified' and a 4px bar, then 'Swift SDK 2.1.0 · last seen 4 min ago'. Windows: name and 'Not seen yet' (dashed ring), then 'Add the SDK →' (Integration's SDK picker, Windows selected). Windows is said once here and nowhere in the cards.
The pane's width is one board column (--board-cols), so its divider lines up with the third card at desktop and wide and the second at tablet: the hero and the board read as one grid.

Each feature card, in canonical order: its service tile and name (the name's link stretches over the card to the feature's home, hover fill, focus ring on the card), the key number at 24/32 and one foot line: Licensing '240 licenses', 'Standard · 3 waiting'; Managed config 'v4 catalog', '12 settings · 3 secrets'; Ship builds '4.2.0 stable', '4.3.0-beta.2 on beta · Oct 6'; Sign-in '312 accounts', 'Pocket ID · members, admins'; Cloud Sync 'Not syncing yet'.
Managed config carries the warning edge and the dot on its tile (aria-label 'Managed config: 1 needs attention'); the problem itself is said once, in the hero.

Integration lives in each card's sunken well: three rows, the same in every card, each an 80px muted label and a state. Console: 'Done', or the open ring and the step as one verb link ('Add Sparkle signing key', 'Set storage per account'). App: 'Drop-in kit' (to that feature on Integration, kit code first), then the quieter 'Your own UI ↗' (aria-label 'Integrate <feature> directly with your own UI: Swift SDK docs'). macOS: Verified with the time only ('Oct 7, 10:42'), 'Waiting for the first sign-in', or 'After the console step'. The rows read in the order the work happens: console, app, platform.

Wells start on one line across a board row (the stat area keeps a value-and-foot height) and every well has the same three rows, so the board scans by row: Done Done Add… / Done Set… across, Verified Verified After… down.
Ship builds' CI publish isn't a row: '4.2.0 stable' and Recent activity ('CI published 4.2.0 to stable') already say CI publishes.

Commerce is off: a dashed card in its canonical sixth place, 'Off' and 'Turn on →' on the line where the other cards' macOS rows sit; the card's link opens the Turn on flow (aria-label 'Commerce: off. Turn on').

When the operator hides Integration, the hero's right pane and every well go; each card becomes a plain stat card (tile, name, number, foot) and the hero is identity and next step only. Hiding is the operator's recorded choice and is reversible from ⋯ More.

Phone: the hero stacks (identity, next step with the full-width primary, then the Integration pane under a hairline). Each card is one line of tile, name and value (the value on the right, as a narrow stat strip), its foot under the name, then the well. Recent activity rows wrap with the time 4px under the text; example-org/djdl never breaks.

Recent activity names the product's events without naming the product: 'Mara Fennick activated a MacBook Pro', 'Tomás Okafor joined as editor'. The DJDL sidebar is unchanged (Devices 412, feature groups as muted labels; the 56px rail at tablet).

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.
B17: the hero's next step, each feature card and activity row carries the service it references; the join row is core.

designReview.reviewer: Senior product designer (exploration B, status board), from the eight renders
designReview.verdict: Concept B replaces the attention card, the integration matrix and the stats strip with one hero and one board: a single focal point (the next step) and six cards that each carry their number and their integration state. Not yet reviewed by the UX panel.

findings.issue: The current Overview has no focal point: Needs attention, a dense integration matrix with Windows floating beside it, and cramped feature tiles all weigh the same.
findings.resolution: The hero band holds identity, the one next step as the page's large primary, and the Integration gauge; everything else is the board.

findings.issue: First render: integration rows differed per card (an open step, a CI row, links pinned to the foot), leaving gaps mid-well and nothing lined up across a row.
findings.resolution: Every well asks the same three questions in the same rows (Console, App, macOS); the CI row is dropped (the 4.2.0 release and Recent activity already show CI publishes).

findings.issue: With data-service on each card, its links took the service accent: five link colours, Managed config's in an amber that read as a warning.
findings.resolution: data-service sits on the icon tile only; links keep the console accent.

findings.issue: Bold platform-name labels in every well made the sunken layer as loud as the numbers above it.
findings.resolution: Well labels are muted regular text with their glyph; the states carry the colour.

findings.issue: Cloud Sync has no foot line, so its well started higher than Sign-in's beside it; on phone it fell into the empty foot row.
findings.resolution: The stat area keeps a value-and-foot height; on phone the well is placed on its own row.

findings.issue: On phone the cards stacked to about 1,100px.
findings.resolution: Phone cards put the value on the name's line (as a narrow stat strip): about 56px less per card.

findings.issue: Repeat 'Windows · Not seen yet' in each card for symmetry with macOS.
findings.resolution: Declined: one platform-level fact, said once in the hero gauge with its 'Add the SDK'; a Windows row appears in the wells once Windows is seen.
